statement: Older adults stop filling heart medicine after their pharmacy closes.
detail: In a 3.1 million-person national cohort of adults 50+, closure caused an immediate significant adherence decline in the first 3 months that persisted a full year.
quote: During the 12 months after pharmacies closed, patients in the closure group had an immediate and significant decline in adherence in the first 3 months compared with those in the control group (absolute change = -5.9%; 95% CI, -6.12 to -5.69).
source_title: Association Between Pharmacy Closures and Adherence to Cardiovascular Medications Among Older US Adults
publisher: JAMA Network Open (via Healio summary of Qato et al.)

statement: Adherence falls for statins, beta-blockers and blood thinners alike.
detail: After a closure, adherence declined similarly across all three cardiovascular drug classes studied in adults 50 and older.
quote: Similar declines in adherence were also seen in patients in the closure group for oral anticoagulants (-5.63%; 95% CI, -6.24 to -5.01) and beta-blockers (-5.71%; 95% CI, -5.96 to -5.46).
source_title: Association Between Pharmacy Closures and Adherence to Cardiovascular Medications Among Older US Adults
publisher: JAMA Network Open (via Healio summary of Qato et al.)

statement: The drop is bigger where pharmacies are already scarce.
detail: Statin adherence fell more steeply after closure for people in low-pharmacy neighborhoods or those who used independent pharmacies.
quote: Patients who filled prescriptions for statin therapy had greater declines in adherence if they lived in neighborhoods with fewer pharmacies (-7.98%; 95% CI, -8.5 to -7.47) or used independent pharmacies (-7.89%; 95% CI, -8.32 to -7.47).
source_title: Association Between Pharmacy Closures and Adherence to Cardiovascular Medications Among Older US Adults
publisher: JAMA Network Open (via Healio summary of Qato et al.)

statement: Over half a million in Massachusetts live in a pharmacy desert.
detail: By the state's own definition, 8.3% of Massachusetts residents already lack convenient pharmacy access in 2025.
quote: 8.3% of the population in Massachusetts, about 580,000 people, currently lives in a pharmacy desert in 2025.
source_title: Over Half a Million Massachusetts Residents Live in a Pharmacy Desert (DataPoints Issue 31)

detail: The state's pharmacy count fell from 1,134 to 940, hitting grocery, small-chain and independent stores hardest.
quote: Since 2019, the number of pharmacies in Massachusetts has decreased by nearly 200 (from 1,134 to 940), a 17.1% decline, with the largest relative decrease for grocery-based pharmacies and small chains and independent pharmacies.
source_title: Over Half a Million Massachusetts Residents Live in a Pharmacy Desert (DataPoints Issue 31)

statement: One in six residents live in a desert or one closure away.
detail: Adding 525,000 people in 'near-deserts' (one pharmacy, whose closure creates a desert) to the 580,000 already in deserts.
quote: In total, over one million Massachusetts residents, 15.8% of the Commonwealth, live in either a pharmacy desert or a 'near-desert.'
source_title: Over Half a Million Massachusetts Residents Live in a Pharmacy Desert (DataPoints Issue 31)

statement: Rite Aid closed every store after two bankruptcies.
detail: A chain that ran more than 2,000 stores as recently as 2023 shut all locations nationwide by October 2025.
quote: Rite Aid, the U.S. pharmacy chain that operated more than 2,000 stores nationwide as recently as 2023, announced Friday it has officially shuttered all of its locations after years of financial struggle.
source_title: Rite Aid shutters all stores after years of financial struggles

statement: Walgreens said it will close 1,200 stores in three years.
detail: Announced on its October 2024 earnings call, including 500 in fiscal 2025, after a $3 billion quarterly loss.
quote: Walgreens will close 500 stores next year, toward the end of the year, and reach a total of 1,200 store closings in the next three years, according to company executives on a fourth quarter earnings call today.
source_title: Walgreens closing 1,200 stores over next 3 years, 800 more under evaluation

statement: CVS planned to close about 900 stores, 2022 to 2024.
detail: Announced in November 2021 at roughly 300 per year, about 9% of its nearly 10,000 U.S. stores.
quote: The company said it plans to close about 300 per year. In total, the closures will add up to roughly 9% of CVS' nearly 10,000 U.S. stores.
source_title: CVS store closures: Company to shut about 300 stores a year over next three years

statement: A third of big-city neighborhoods are pharmacy deserts.
detail: Across the 30 largest U.S. cities (2007-2015), with 8.3 million Black and Latino residents living in deserts.
quote: One in three neighborhoods throughout these cities were pharmacy deserts, affecting nearly 15 million people... limited access to pharmacies disproportionately impacts racial/ethnic minorities - 8.3 million Black and Latino residents of these cities live in deserts.
source_title: Fewer Pharmacies In Black And Hispanic/Latino Neighborhoods Compared With White Or Diverse Neighborhoods, 2007-15 (USC Schaeffer summary of Guadamuz et al.)

statement: Nearly 3 in 10 U.S. pharmacies closed over a decade.
detail: Of 88,930 retail pharmacies operating 2010-20, 29.4% had closed by 2021, with independent and Black/Latinx-neighborhood stores most at risk.
quote: We found that of the 88,930 retail pharmacies operating during 2010-20, 29.4 percent had closed by 2021. The risk for closure for pharmacies in predominantly Black and Latinx neighborhoods was higher than in White neighborhoods.
source_title: More US Pharmacies Closed Than Opened In 2018-21; Independent Pharmacies, Those In Black, Latinx Communities Most At Risk
publisher: Health Affairs (Guadamuz et al., via PMC)

statement: Not taking medicines costs the U.S. up to $300B a year.
detail: CDC figure for direct health-care costs of medication non-adherence, tied to higher hospitalizations and worse outcomes.
quote: Whereas rates of non-adherence across the United States have remained relatively stable, direct health care costs associated with nonadherence have grown to approximately $100-$300 billion of U.S. health care dollars spent annually.
source_title: CDC Grand Rounds: Improving Medication Adherence for Chronic Disease Management
